annotations.text: Direction A built out with a glass finish. Two levers above the board: Glass blur dials the frost, Glass tint sets the panel colour. Case data is sample data. The three direction sketches are kept on the Directions page.

A · Canvas first (chosen)
The graph takes every pixel between the rail and the inspector. All graph controls collapse into one floating toolbar; the entity list floats on the canvas and collapses; one command bar replaces the page header and both add forms.
Why: fixes the small-graph and scroll problems directly, with the least change to what people already know.
Tradeoff: more controls sit behind toggles, and relationship review still lives on another view.

B · Investigation desk
Three fixed panes: ledger, graph, inspector with Entity / Relationships / Evidence tabs. The whole loop (add, pivot, review, cite) happens on one screen; five views collapse to two.
Why: no navigation for the core loop, and the review queue is always in sight.
Tradeoff: needs a wide display, each pane is narrower, and the overview's metrics and lead triage lose their own page.

C · Guided queue
The home screen is a task list of things needing a decision. The selected item opens in the centre with accept and reject; the graph is a preview that expands on demand; a four-step strip shows where you are.
Why: friendliest for a first-time user and for analysts who work by decisions rather than by graph. The empty case becomes the same screen with the first steps open.
Tradeoff: the graph is secondary, and power users click more to get to it.
